content: Blackfriars printer from Stratford; lends his 1587 Holinshed
Prints North's Plutarch (1595) and supplies Rochelle paper
He will not enter a day on a wet step while the apprentices can hear it.
He can offer a smaller Venus with not a penny in it, and ask for the comedy in the same call, and disapprove of it.
He called plays a waste with a crowd in it, lent the second volume, and said he will see the gap on the shelf every morning until it is home.
The grace is long and the carving is short. He asks after the chronicle and lets it go. He says he is your friend, and then he tells you to leave the book.
Fourteen shillings, unbound. Whitsun asked, and not got. An error acquires company. Thursday is market day at home whether or not he is there.
He wants the anger at his table, and he wants the Holinshed, and he can be given the first without the second.
He wants the comedy for the press, and he already knows the copy is not William's to give.
He will take a book back and leave a lent chronicle named as lent, in under a minute.
The horse is always dear to him, and his Holinshed does not travel.
He wants the second volume back, and when the great house by the chapel goes by in a list he looks up and lets it pass.
The margin, by his account, is for the poems, and a player is wasted on the day he is played.
A proverb will not hide a question from him, and he will not price the thing you asked about in order to let you escape.
A plain "no, not yet" is more useful to him than a flourish, and his chronicle is still at Great St Helen's.
